thread:
mike: noticing a spike in reconnects for long SSE streams this morning, looks correlated with a shard reassign at 02:14 UTC. clients see a resume, then a second reconnect 200ms later and we bill both. logs: `resume_id=abc123, route=us-west-2-a, shard=pool-7 -> pool-12, latency=240ms`
anya: ugh. do we have a reproducible test?
sam: i can repro with a script that holds the stream open for ~45s and triggers a route flip. i'll share it.
mike: repro script would be great. also console shows two active sockets for the same token for ~1s, then one goes away. looks like our routing sticky-lease and resume path are racing.
liz: is the duplicate billing from two simultaneous active sessions or from resume+reconnect idempotency missing?
mike: both. token-level meter shows two in-flight connections for same token, billing backend counts both since the resume transition isn't annotated as a continuation.
telemetry-bot: note: we currently tag events with `session_id` and `route_id` but not `resume_reason` or `reconnect_phase`. makes it hard to separate planned handoffs vs client re-opens.
anya: propose adding a `reconnect_reason` enum (planned_handoff, proxy_restart, client_backoff, resume_failure) and include a `resume_parent_id` to link the two sockets. would help console dedupe.
sam: quick patch idea: when we detect a resume token claim on a new route within 1s of previous session expiry, emit `resume_parent_id` and set meter to attribute tokens to parent until new session ack. but need to be careful for stuck parent.
liz: does quota enforcement rely on unique conn ids? if we start attributing to parent we might undercount bursts.
mike: correct. need a windowed attribution: attribute to parent for N ms or until parent reports terminal close, whichever first. N=1500ms?
anya: for safety, make N configurable per tier and expose heuristic in console. e.g., "resume_attribution_window_ms" with default 1500.
telemetry-bot: also add metric `resume_success_rate` (by route, model, tenant) and `duplicate_connection_charge_count`. both are currently absent.
liz: rollout plan? this needs to touch runtime, gateway, billing emitter, and console. I'd like a canary for runtime/gateway first with telemetry only (no billing attribution) to validate tagging.
mike: agreed. canary gates: 1) runtime emits new tags, 2) gateway consumes tags and sets `resume_parent_id`, 3) billing is disabled for attribution until we validate metrics for 24h.
deploy-bot: deploy plan created: PR 4821 (runtime telemetry) -> canary group us-west-2-a (5% traffic) -> monitor `resume_success_rate` and `duplicate_connection_charge_count` for 6h.
san: typo: PR reviewer assigned to sam.
sam: i'll review. also adding repro script to `internal/tools/stream-repro` and a harness that flips routing table on demand.
anya: console UX: surface a small badge on connection panel when a session is "possible resume" (high-confidence link) with a link to the raw resume events. that will help support triage.
liz: agree. also add an alert rule: if `duplicate_connection_charge_count` > 5 in 1m for a tenant, page the oncall.
mike: last thought: can we avoid the short double-open by delaying socket final-close on previous route for 500ms until new route confirms resume claim? might reduce tail latency but could also increase connection churn at proxies. tradeoff.
anya: maybe implement as a soft hold with backpressure: keep previous server accepting but mark as "handoff_pending" and drop payloads after 1s. we'll need small changes to proxy layer.
sam: ok i'll prototype. for now, let's push telemetry-first as planned.
deploy-bot: canary started for PR 4821 on us-west-2-a at 6930008200. monitoring window 6h.
mike: thanks team — keeping this in the eng-platform thread. please paste any console screenshots or short logs here as you validate.
